messages:
sanjay: Heads up — integrating the JS SDK with a customer's VPC/private endpoint + corporate proxy. Need clarity on precedence for base URL, proxy env vars, and mTLS. Quick questions:
1) if REDWOOD_API_BASE is set and client init passes baseUrl, which wins?
2) For VPC/private, do we require SNI match on proxy?
3) streaming over proxy: chunked responses get buffered — known issue?

emma: Quick answer: explicit constructor param > env var > SDK default. For (2) we require SNI for TLS passthrough; if the proxy terminates TLS and does mTLS there, SNI isn't required. For (3) yes, some proxies buffer chunks. More details below.

kai: Node snippet for passing baseUrl + agent:
```
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  baseUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_API_BASE || 'https://api.redwood.example',
  fetch,
  agent: proxyAgent // e.g. https-proxy-agent or custom https.Agent
});
```

jen: Streaming + proxies: common culprits are buffering and HTTP/1.1 proxy implementations. Nginx/Envoy default configs can buffer. Workaround: disable buffering (`proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off;`) or use HTTP/2/GRPC if supported. Also ensure `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` is preserved by the proxy.

emma: mTLS details: for Private installs we expect client certs. Set REDWOOD_CLIENT_CERT_PATH and REDWOOD_CLIENT_KEY_PATH or pass cert/key via agent. In node you can attach to https.Agent: `{ cert: fs.readFileSync(...), key: ... }`.

kai: Host header precedence note: explicit `Host` header you set on the request wins. SDK will not override Host unless you pass `forceHost` option. So prefer setting baseUrl and let SDK derive Host unless you have special routing.

zach: Perf tip: when going through a proxy, enable keep-alive to avoid repeated TLS handshakes: `new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 50 })` and reuse the agent across requests.

sanjay: Thanks — can someone paste a minimal curl + mTLS example and a python `requests` snippet I can give to the customer?

jen: curl mTLS example:
```
curl --cert client.pem --key client.key -H "Host: private.redwood.local" https://proxy.internal/path
```

emma: Python requests example:
```
import requests
s = requests.Session()
s.verify = '/etc/ssl/ca.pem'
s.cert = ('/path/cert.pem','/path/key.pem')
s.headers.update({'Host':'private.redwood.local'})
resp = s.post('https://proxy.internal/path', json={...})
```
